description: Figure 3 is a composite 3 × 3 array of field-emission SEM (FESEM) micrographs of the Fe–10Al–15Mn–0.8C–5Ni wt% low-density steel annealed at 900 °C. Columns are labelled A5 (5 min), A15 (15 min) and A30 (30 min); the left margin is labelled "lower magnification" for row 1 and "higher magnification" for rows 2 and 3. Row 1 (a–c) carries 5 µm scale bars; rows 2 (d–f) and 3 (g–i) carry 1 µm scale bars. In (a–c) yellow arrows mark elongated "B2 stringer bands" aligned along the prior rolling direction and "URE-γ" pancake-shaped grains, both of which persist at all three annealing times. The higher-magnification panels resolve two precipitate morphologies: blue arrows mark fine needle-like intragranular "IG-B2" (d–f), and green arrows mark coarse, irregular intergranular "GB-B2" located on grain boundaries (d, f–i). Following d→e→f, the IG-B2 needles inside shear bands become longer and thicker, appearing as larger coalesced needles in A30; GB-B2 remains coarse and blocky in (g–i). The group thus demonstrates that three B2 morphologies coexist after annealing — stringer bands, intragranular needles and intergranular particles — and that IG-B2 coarsens while the elongated URE-γ pancake structure survives. No numeric values are printed anywhere except the scale bars.

subfigures.description: Lower-magnification FESEM of sample A5 (5 min anneal), 5 µm scale bar. Yellow arrows label elongated 'B2 stringer bands' lying along the rolling direction and 'URE-γ' regions; the matrix shows a banded, deformed (pancake) structure.

Higher-magnification FESEM of A5, 1 µm scale bar. Green arrows label coarse blocky 'GB-B2' at grain boundaries; blue arrows label fine 'IG-B2' needles inside the grain interior.
Higher-magnification FESEM of A15, 1 µm scale bar. Blue arrows label 'IG-B2' needles; green arrows label coarse 'GB-B2' particles along boundaries; a thick prolate band crosses the field.

Higher-magnification FESEM of A30, 1 µm scale bar. Blue arrows label 'IG-B2'; needles are conspicuously longer and thicker here than in (d), consistent with growth/coalescence; green arrows mark 'GB-B2'.
Higher-magnification FESEM of A5, 1 µm scale bar. Green arrows label coarse blocky/irregular 'GB-B2' particles sitting on grain boundaries within a smooth matrix.

Higher-magnification FESEM of A30, 1 µm scale bar. Green arrows label angular, coarse 'GB-B2' particles on boundaries; a few finer elongated IG-B2 needles are also visible in the matrix.

observations.observation: Figure 3 is a 3 × 3 array of FESEM micrographs, with column headings A5, A15 and A30 and row labels 'lower magnification' (row 1) and 'higher magnification' (rows 2 and 3).
Scale bars are 5 µm in the lower-magnification row (a–c) and 1 µm in the higher-magnification rows (d–i).
Yellow arrows label 'B2 stringer bands' elongated parallel to the prior rolling direction in (a), (b) and (c).
Yellow arrows label 'URE-γ' pancake-shaped elongated grains in (a) and (b).
Blue arrows label fine needle-like 'IG-B2' precipitates in the higher-magnification panels (d), (e) and (f).
Green arrows label coarse, blocky/irregular 'GB-B2' particles located on grain boundaries in (d), (f), (g), (h) and (i).
IG-B2 needles appear longer and thicker in A30 (f) than in A5 (d) at the same 1 µm scale, consistent with growth and coalescence with annealing time.
The caption states the panels correspond to annealing for a,d,g) 5 min, b,e,h) 15 min and c,f,i) 30 min, and that URE-γ is uncrystallized austenite maintaining a pancake structure.
The citing text states the IG-B2 nucleates within unrecrystallized-γ (URE-γ) containing shear bands, which act as heterogeneous nucleation sites (Figure 3a–f).

The citing text asserts that intragranular precipitation of BCC second-phase particles in the fully recrystallized γ (RE-γ) grain body was negligible (Figure 3g); no RE-γ label or recrystallized-grain annotation is visible in the pixels to confirm this.

The citing text states IG-B2 is finer in A5 and grows into a needle shape through mutual coalescence in shear bands during 30 min annealing (Figure 3d–f), while coarse GB-B2 results from enhanced solute flux from grain-boundary regions (Figure 3g–i).
The citing text states that the RE-γ grain size increases with annealing time and that URE-γ grains stay coarse and elongated along the prior RD in the pancake structure (Figure 3a–c).

The citing text reports IG-B2 sizes/fractions used with this figure: D_IG-B2 = 0.29 µm with f_IG-B2 = 1.1% in RE-γ giving 23 MPa, and IG-B2 of 0.2 µm at 2.6% in URE-γ giving 43 MPa, totalling 66 MPa of precipitation strengthening; these numbers are not printed on the figure.
The citing text states that B2, GB-B2 and B2 stringer bands are the three B2 morphologies retained after annealing, and that B2 inhibits γ recrystallization.

unreadable_items: No numeric data values (sizes, fractions or properties) are printed on any panel; only the 5 µm and 1 µm scale bars are readable, so all precipitate dimensions must be judged relative to those bars.
Panels (g)–(i) are lower in contrast and the arrow labels are placed on smooth matrix areas; the exact arrow targets are only partially decidable.
RE-γ (fully recrystallized γ) is named in the caption/citation but is not labelled in the pixels, so its identification in (g) cannot be confirmed.
